analysis:
The supplied units are base-side excerpts of desktop-app/package-lock.json (lines 822-2448), and the patch excerpt is truncated. Visible changes are dev-only dependency bumps: electron 44.5.1 to 44.9.1, vite 8.3.2 to 8.3.5, @oxc-project/types 0.152.0 to 0.155.0, and the @rolldown/binding-* packages 1.2.12 to 1.2.15, plus added lines around head 1869-2018 (likely more rolldown bindings). In the excerpt, the new resolved URLs point at registry.npmjs.org and new sha512 integrity hashes are present, so I saw no registry-host swaps or removed integrity fields. The rest of the changes (head ranges 3679-6703, including 5998-6028 and other regions) are not visible, so I could not review them.

Nothing in the visible lockfile content touches the threat-model assets or boundaries: the provider WebSocket contract (TB-002), the operator-versus-process boundary (TB-003), App Attest authorization (TB-011), the attestation chain (TB-009), or the keys. The desktop-app is a console/consumer-side build tool, and these are dev dependencies. Electron is a build-time dev dependency here, but the packaged desktop app could carry it, so the version bump is security-relevant only as a patch update and is not a regression.

Remaining questions for integration: the truncated hunks (head 3679+, 5998-6028) were not seen and could contain unrelated dependency changes. The package.json counterpart should be checked to confirm the lockfile matches the manifest. No finding is supported by the supplied evidence.
